newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: OLYMPICS-FIFA OFFICIAL TO HEAD SWISS WINTER OLYMPIC BID.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-FIFA OFFICIAL TO HEAD SWISS WINTER OLYMPIC BID.

text.p: Sepp Blatter, general secretary of the international football body FIFA, was on Friday appointed to head a bid by the Swiss city of Sion to win the 2006 Winter Olympics.
Blatter's appointment as president of the committee to organise the bid was approved by the Swiss cabinet, an official announcement said.
There was no immediate comment from FIFA but it was believed Blatter, who has been tipped as a possible successor to long-serving FIFA president Joao Havelange, would keep his post there.
Swiss diplomat and former ambassador to France Edouard Brunner was named head of international relations for the committee -- Sion 2006.

The picturesque 1,000-year-old capital of the mountain- fringed Valais canton along the upper reaches of the River Rhone lost an earlier bid for the 2002 Games, which were awarded to Salt Lake City in the United States.

Formal bids for the 2006 Games have to be lodged with the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in Lausanne by January next year. A shortlist of candidates will be chosen a year later and the winner will be named in September 1999.
